extracted.intended_audience: readers of 18th-century English fiction; writers/students examining Sterne's comic-digressive style
extracted.subtask_description: A passage from Laurence Sterne's Tristram Shandy containing an embedded 'letter of instructions' (comic prescriptive advice on courtship) and narrated planning scenes; useful for studying comic, digressive prose and period-specific behavioral prescriptions. Extracts practical maxims and theatrical 'rubric'-like injunctions embedded in fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious preface / invocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Never to go forth upon the enterprize, whether it be in the morning or the afternoon, without first recommending thyself to the protection of Almighty God, that he may defend thee from the evil one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treats a devout invocation as a necessary precursor to any courtship undertaking; positioned as a protective ritual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep baldness out of her fancy (grooming)
rubrics_metrics.description: Shave the whole top of thy crown clean once at least every four or five days, but oftner if convenient; lest in taking off thy wig before her, thro’ absence of mind, she should be able to discover how much has been cut away by Time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical grooming rule framed as preventing awkward revelations: 'Twere better to keep ideas of baldness out of her fancy.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt maxim: 'women are timid'
rubrics_metrics.description: Always carry it in thy mind, and act upon it as a sure maxim, Toby — 'That women are timid:' And ’tis well they are — else there would be no dealing with them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A behavioural principle recommending a deferential, cautious approach to women in courtship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breeches fit: aim for a just medium
rubrics_metrics.description: Let not thy breeches be too tight, or hang too loose about thy thighs. — A just medium prevents all conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical dress-advice emphasizing moderation in clothing to avoid improper impressions or practical impediments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speak softly; cultivate silence
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever thou hast to say, be it more or less, forget not to utter it in a low soft tone of voice. Silence, and whatever approaches it, weaves dreams of midnight secrecy into the brain: For this cause, if thou canst help it, never throw down the tongs and poker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tone and silence to create intimacy and secrecy; avoid abrupt domestic actions that break mood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pleasantry and discourage laughter-inducing reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid all kinds of pleasantry and facetiousness in thy discourse with her, and do whatever lies in thy power at the same time, to keep her from all books and writings which tend thereto: there are some devotional tracts, which if thou canst entice her to read over — it will be well: but suffer her not to look into Rabelais, or Scarron, or Don Quixote — They are all books which excite laughter; and thou knowest, dear Toby, that there is no passion so serious as lust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribes steering the lady toward serious/devotional reading and away from comic works to avoid stimulating levity linked to sexual desire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-entry small ritual (pin in shirt)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stick a pin in the bosom of thy shirt, before thou enterest her parlour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A small affectation or superstition prescribed to regulate appearance or comportment before meeting her.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid taking her hand prematurely
rubrics_metrics.description: And if thou art permitted to sit upon the same sopha with her, and she gives thee occasion to lay thy hand upon hers — beware of taking it — thou canst not lay thy hand on hers, but she will feel the temper of thine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns that physical contact communicates temperament; counsel to refrain from seizing opportunities for touch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep things undetermined to provoke curiosity
rubrics_metrics.description: Leave that and as many other things as thou canst, quite undetermined; by so doing, thou wilt have her curiosity on thy side; and if she is not conquered by that...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tactical advice: ambiguity and restraint increase curiosity and attraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bloodletting as a remedy for intemperate appetite
rubrics_metrics.description: Thou must begin, with first losing a few ounces of blood below the ears, according to the practice of the ancient Scythians, who cured the most intemperate fits of the appetite by that means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Period medical-cum-behavioural prescription for checking uncontrolled desire; presented as an historical remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avicenna / hellebore treatment and purges
rubrics_metrics.description: Avicenna, after this, is for having the part anointed with the syrup of hellebore, using proper evacuations and purges — and I believe rightly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further period-medical measures recommended to moderate impulses; part of the same medical regimen as bloodletting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dietary prohibitions to moderate desire
rubrics_metrics.description: Thou must eat little or no goat’s flesh, nor red deer — nor even foal’s flesh by any means; and carefully abstain — that is, as much as thou canst, from peacocks, cranes, coots, didappers, and water-hens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists specific meats and birds to avoid as part of managing bodily humours and sexual appetite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prescribed drinks and restorative foods
rubrics_metrics.description: As for thy drink — it must be the infusion of VERVAIN and the herb HANEA, of which Ælian relates such effects — but if thy stomach palls with it — discontinue it from time to time, taking cucumbers, melons, purslane, water-lillies, woodbine, and lettice, in the stead of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies herbal infusions as the proper drink, with fallback to cooling vegetables/greens if the regimen is intolerable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grooming & attire preparation for the 'attack' (military plan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures taken: get your honour’s laced clothes out of the great campaign-trunk, to be well air’d, have the blue and gold taken up at the sleeves, put your white ramallie-wig fresh into pipes, send for a taylor to have your thin scarlet breeches turn’d; two razors shall be new set; furbish your Montero cap; put on poor lieutenant Le Fever’s regimental coat; be clean shaved and have a clean shirt on, with your blue and gold, or your fine scarlet — sometimes one and sometimes t’other — and every thing ready for the attack — we’ll march up boldly, as if ’twas to the face of a bastion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A theatrical, quasi-military checklist for appearance and timing before carrying out a courtship 'attack'; emphasizes coordinated grooming, clothing, and boldness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate roles & seize the pass (campaign metaphor for courtship)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whilst your honour engages Mrs. Wadman in the parlour, to the right — I’ll attack Mrs. Bridget in the kitchen, to the left; and having seiz’d the pass, I’ll answer for it ... that the day is our own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribes a coordinated, two-pronged approach to courting akin to military maneuvers: divided responsibilities and synchronous action to secure success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose non-clumsy clothing for the enterprise
rubrics_metrics.description: I had better take the red plush ones, quoth my uncle Toby — They will be too clumsy — said the corporal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical sartorial advice to avoid garments that impede movement or decorum; choose suitable, non-clumsy attire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character & gentleness can elevate outward appearance
rubrics_metrics.description: The sweet look of goodness which sat upon my uncle Toby’s [face]... assimilated every thing around it so sovereignly to itself, ... that even his tarnish’d gold-laced hat and huge cockade of flimsy taffeta became him; and though not worth a button in themselves, yet the moment my uncle Toby put them on, they became serious objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An evaluative note: personal virtue, gentleness and gentlemanliness make outward defects seem becoming — inner character modifies perception of external dress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid peeping through key-holes (moral injunction)
rubrics_metrics.description: The mistake in my father, was in attacking my mother’s motive, instead of the act itself; for certainly key-holes were made for other purposes; and considering the act, as an act which interfered with a true proposition, and denied a key-hole to be what it was — it became a violation of nature; and was so far, you see, criminal. It is for this reason... That key-holes are the occasions of more sin and wickedness, than all other holes in this world put together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A moral maxim discouraging voyeuristic curiosity; framed as both natural and criminal transgression.
